fact: Shape models: Didymos v003 and Dimorphos v004 from DART DRACO and LICIACube LUKE images (body-fixed, km, +Z = north pole). Used: Didymos 4.657 m and Dimorphos 0.972 m global OBJs.

sources.t: Daly et al., DART Shapemodel Archive Bundle, PDS SBN (2023), doi:10.26007/96fn-p578

fact: Didymos model extent 818 × 802 × 605 m (flattened at the poles, a spinning-top shape); DRACO imaging of Didymos was limited to about 3.7 m resolution; Didymos pole RA 66.83°, Dec −73.0° (ICRF).

sources.t: DART: Didymos coordinate system description v1 (PDS)

fact: Post-impact orbit of Dimorphos: period 11.3674 ± 0.0004 h (after settling from 11.377 h), eccentricity 0.0274 ± 0.0015; Didymos pole ecliptic latitude −80.7 ± 0.5° (so the orbit is retrograde, inclined about 170.7° to the ecliptic).

sources.t: Naidu et al. 2024, PSJ: Orbital and physical characterization of Dimorphos following the DART impact

fact: Post-impact semi-major axis 1.144 ± 0.070 km; period 11 h 22 m 03 s.
Dimorphos model extent 178 × 169 × 115 m. Its rotation after the DART impact is under study (possible non-synchronous or tumbling state), which Hera will measure.

sources.t: BAAS 56(6): The Rotational State of Dimorphos After the DART Impact (DDA 2024)
